advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Close proc.stdout/proc.stderr (or route the success path through a drain that closes the pipes) after _read_limited returns so pipe fds are not leaked per invocation.
evidence: `.close()` search over terraform_corroborator.py returns (no matches) — nothing closes proc.stdout/proc.stderr on the success path
Prior code used `stdout, stderr = proc.communicate(timeout=DEADLINE_SECONDS)`, and communicate() closes the pipe fds; the replacement only wait()s
_run's finally clause only calls shutil.rmtree(home, ...), not any pipe close (src/rebar/grounding/terraform_corroborator.py:325-326)
advisory.finding: On the success path, _read_limited returns after proc.wait() without ever closing proc.stdout/proc.stderr. The prior code used proc.communicate(), which closes both pipe file objects. Now the two pipe file descriptors remain open after each successful corroboration until the Popen object is garbage-collected, leaking two fds per invocation.
scenarios: Repeated corroborate_diagnostic calls within a long-lived session accumulate open pipe fds until GC runs, risking fd exhaustion under sustained grounding load
advisory.suggested_fix: In _read_limited, close the pipes before returning, e.g. wrap the read loop so that proc.stdout.close() and proc.stderr.close() run in a finally, or call proc.wait() and then close both file objects explicitly.
